**Finding: Compliant** (rule MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer)

No most-favoured-nation obligation burdens Ono anywhere in the agreement. I checked the planner's candidates and ran searches across the usual MFN formulations — "most favored/favoured nation", "no less favorable", "as favorable", "more favorable", "better terms", "best price", plus matching-right analogues ("first refusal", "match") — and found nothing requiring Ono to extend Array terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers.

The two closest analogues both run **in our favour**, so per the rule's direction guidance they are not flagged:

- **p0502** protects Ono: Array may not require Ono to place direct Subcontractor orders unless the Subcontractor will fulfil them "on terms as favorable to Ono as the terms such Subcontractors have extended to Array."
- **p0190** obliges Array to use Diligent Efforts to pass Third Party Partner clinical data, know-how, rights of reference and improvements through to Ono, without charge.

The only other "favorable" hit (p0476) is a routine withholding-tax provision, not an MFN.

This sits at the **preferred** position, so no redline was proposed.
